caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 429 of 2008.
lawyer:
Md Ibrahim Khalil, Advocate-on-Record-----For the Petitioner.
Not Represented-----For the Respondents.
parties:
Abdul Jabbar ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Akter Hossain Bhuiyan and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment: "Mr Md Shafiqul Islam Dhali the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite-party in reply submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, firstly committed error of law in misreading the Exhibit 3, registered deed of sale dated 1-8-1989 executed by CS recorded Zamindar Akkas Uddin in favour of Hazetun Nessa transferring the rent receiving interest of the suit land along with other land, inasmuch as, the same being a registered deed of sale executed and registered about 90 years old and negative presumption of the same could only be formed through evidence keeping in view of the development and circumstances consequent to the execution and registration thereof till the present. Mr. Dhali next submits that the plaintiffs exhibited as many as 20 rent receipts out of them some were issued by Zaminder and 18 of them issued by the Government, being Exhibit 4 series proved the payment of rent in respect of the suit land till 1988 by the plaintiff and also proved the possession and enjoyment of the suit property by the plaintiffs and further standing of collateral evidence of title of the plaintiffs in support of his contention, but the learned Sub-ordinate Judge in his judgment mentioned that the plaintiffs exhibited only 2 rent receipt and thereby proceeded towards by the erroneous decision in support of his contention Mr Dhali relies on the decision of our. Appellate Division reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216 wherein it has been held that rent receipts through not documents of title, are not items of evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows of title. Mr Dhali further submits that SA Khatian being Exhibits Kha(2) and Kha(3) and RS Khatian finally published being recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs and in the name of the plaintiffs respectively although one of the two SA Khatian being Exhibit Kha(2) contained the name of the CS recorded tenants along with the name of the predecessors of the plaintiff. In this connection Mr Dhali submits that it is settled principle of law that the last record of right will prevail than the earlier record of right, in support of his contention he relies on the decision reported in 35 DLR 295 and 17 DLR 392 and 27 DLR 589 relying on the decision of a Division Bench of this Court reported in 42 DLR 434. Mr Dhali submits that RS Khatian prepared under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has the presumption of correctness under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Mr Dhali finally submits that although the judgment of the learned Additional District Judge is not lengthy but the learned Additional District Judge refers the Judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge adverting the material findings of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and discussed the oral and documentary evidence in doing so and that there is no misreading of any evidence on record and neither there is any non-consideration of material evidence on record on the part of the learned Additional District Judge and that being so the Additional District Judge being appellate Court and thereby being the final Court of facts, its judgment is not liable to be interfered with."
